'''Japaridze's polymodal logic''' ('''GLP''') is a system of [[provability logic]] with infinitely many provability [[modal logic|modalities]]. This system has played an important role 
in some applications of provability algebras in [[proof theory]], and has been extensively studied since the late 1980s. It is named after [[Giorgi Japaridze]].

== Language and axiomatization ==

The language of GLP extends that of the language of classical [[propositional logic]] by including the infinite series {{math|1=[0],[1],[2],...}} of necessity operators. Their dual possibility operators {{math|1=<0>,<1>,<2>,...}} are defined by {{math|1=<''n''>''p'' = ¬[''n'']¬''p''}}.

The axioms of GLP are all classical tautologies and all formulas of one of the following forms:
*{{math|1=[''n''](''p'' → ''q'') → ([''n'']''p'' → [''n'']''q'')}}
*{{math|1=[''n'']([''n'']''p'' → ''p'') → [''n'']''p''}}
*{{math|1=[''n'']''p'' → [''n''+1]''p''}}
*{{math|1=<''n''>''p'' → [''n''+1]<''n''>''p''}}

And the rules of inference are:
* From  {{math|1=''p''}} and {{math|''p'' → ''q''}} conclude {{math|1=''q''}}
* From  {{math|1=''p''}} conclude {{math|1=[0]''p''}}

== Provability semantics ==

Consider a sufficiently strong [[first-order theory]] {{math|1=''T''}} such as [[Peano Arithmetic]] {{math|1=''PA''}}. 
Define the series {{math|1=''T''<sub>0</sub>,''T''<sub>1</sub>,''T''<sub>2</sub>,...}} of theories as follows:
*{{math|1=''T''<sub>0</sub>}} is {{math|1=''T''}}
*{{math|1=''T''<sub>''n''+1</sub>}} is the extension of {{math|1=''T''<sub>''n''</sub>}} through the additional axioms {{math|1=∀''xF''(''x'')}} for each formula {{math|1=''F''(''x'')}} such that {{math|1=''T''<sub>''n''</sub>}} proves all of the formulas  {{math|1=''F''(0), ''F''(1), ''F''(2),...}}

For each {{math|1=''n''}}, let {{math|1=Pr<sub>''n''</sub>(''x'')}} be a natural arithmetization of the predicate 
{{math|1="''x''}} is the [[Gödel number]] of a sentence provable in {{math|1=''T''<sub>''n''</sub>"}}.

A ''realization'' is a function {{math|1=*}} that sends each nonlogical atom {{math|1=''a''}} of
the language of GLP to a sentence {{math|1=''a''*}} of the language of {{math|1=''T''}}. It extends to all formulas
of the language of GLP by stipulating that {{math|1=*}} commutes with the Boolean connectives, and 
that {{math|1=([''n'']''F'')*}} is {{math|1=Pr<sub>''n''</sub>('<nowiki/>''F''*')}}, where {{math|1='<nowiki/>''F''*'}}
stands for (the numeral for) the Gödel number of {{math|1=''F''*}}.

An arithmetical completeness theorem<ref name="japaridze1988">G. Japaridze, [http://www.csc.villanova.edu/~japaridz/1988PolymodalProvLog.pdf "The polymodal logic of provability"]. ''Intensional Logics and Logical Structure of Theories''. Metsniereba, Tbilisi, 1988, pp. 16–48 (Russian).</ref> for GLP states that a formula {{math|1=''F''}} is provable in GLP [[if and only if]], for every interpretation {{math|1=*}}, the sentence {{math|1=''F''*}} is provable in {{math|1=''T''}}.

The above understanding of the series {{math|1=''T''<sub>0</sub>,''T''<sub>1</sub>,''T''<sub>2</sub>,...}} of theories is not the only natural understanding yielding the soundness and completeness of GLP. For instance, each theory {{math|1=''T''<sub>''n''</sub>}} can be understood as {{math|1=''T''}} augmented with all true {{math|1=Π<sub>n</sub>}} sentences as additional axioms. [[George Boolos]] showed<ref>G. Boolos, [http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/016800729390200W "The analytical completeness of Japaridze's polymodal logics"]. ''Annals of Pure and Applied Logic'' 61 (1993), pp. 95–111.</ref> that GLP remains sound and complete with analysis ([[second-order arithmetic]]) in the role of the base theory {{math|1=''T''}}.

== Other semantics ==

GLP has been shown<ref name="japaridze1988" /> to be incomplete with respect to any class of [[Kripke frame]]s.

A natural topological semantics of GLP interprets modalities as derivative operators of a [[polytopological space]]. Such spaces are called 
GLP-spaces whenever they satisfy all the axioms of GLP. GLP is complete with respect to the class of all GLP-spaces.<ref name="beklemishev2013">L. Beklemishev and  D. Gabelaia, [http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168007213000778 "Topological completeness of provability logic GLP"]. ''Annals of Pure and Applied Logic'' 164 (2013), pp. 1201–1223.</ref>

== Computational complexity ==

The problem of being a theorem of GLP is [[PSPACE-complete]]. So is the same problem restricted to only variable-free formulas of GLP.<ref name="pakhomov2014">F. Pakhomov, [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs00153-014-0397-4 "On the complexity of the closed fragment of Japaridze's provability logic"]. ''Archive for Mathematical Logic'' 53 (2014), pp. 949–967.</ref>

== History ==

GLP, under the name GP, was introduced by [[Giorgi Japaridze]] in his PhD thesis "Modal Logical Means of Investigating Provability" ([[Moscow State University]], 1986) and published two years later<ref name="japaridze1988" /> along with (a) the [[Gödel's completeness theorem|completeness theorem]] for GLP with respect to its provability interpretation (Beklemishev subsequently came up with a simpler proof of the same theorem<ref>L. Beklemishev, [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1134%2FS0081543811060046 "A simplified proof of arithmetical completeness theorem for provability logic GLP"]. ''Proceedings of the Steklov Institute of Mathematics'' 274 (2011),  pp. 25–33.</ref>) and (b) a proof that Kripke frames for GLP do not exist. Beklemishev also conducted a more extensive study of Kripke models for GLP.<ref>L. Beklemishev, [http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S016800720900116X "Kripke semantics for provability logic GLP"]. ''Annals of Pure and Applied Logic'' 161, 756–774 (2010).</ref> 
Topological models for GLP were studied by Beklemishev, Bezhanishvili, Icard and Gabelaia.<ref name="beklemishev2013" /><ref>L. Beklemishev, G. Bezhanishvili and T. Icard,  "On topological models of GLP". ''Ways of proof theory, Ontos Mathematical Logic'', 2, eds. R. Schindler, Ontos Verlag, Frankfurt, 2010, pp. 133–153.
</ref>
The decidability of GLP in polynomial space was proven by  I. Shapirovsky,<ref>I. Shapirovsky, [http://www.aiml.net/volumes/volume7/Shapirovsky.pdf "PSPACE-decidability of Japaridze's polymodal logic"]. ''Advances in Modal Logic'' 7 (2008), pp. 289-304.</ref> and the PSPACE-hardness of its variable-free fragment was proven by  F. Pakhomov.<ref name="pakhomov2014" /> Among the most notable applications of GLP has been its use in  proof-theoretically analyzing  [[Peano arithmetic]], elaborating a canonical way for recovering [[ordinal  notation]]  up to {{math|1=ɛ<sub>0</sub>}} from  the  corresponding  algebra, and constructing simple combinatorial independent statements  (Beklemishev <ref>L. Beklemishev, [http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168007203001325 "Provability algebras and proof-theoretic ordinals, I"]. ''Annals of Pure and Applied Logic'' 128 (2004), pp. 103–123.</ref>).

An extensive survey of GLP in the context of provability logics in general was given by [[George Boolos]] in his book ''The Logic of Provability''.<ref>G. Boolos, ''[https://www.amazon.com/The-Logic-Provability-George-Boolos/dp/0521483255 The Logic of Provability]''. Cambridge University Press, 1993.</ref>
